clue.text: Miner runs out for dog

indicators.note: out tells us the runs letter goes missing from the miner word

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A coal miner leaves his job to look after a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs out' reads as the miner fleeing, but it says the R for runs is taken out of COLLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Got passed (caught me in tight bay)

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in places the word me inside the jumbled bay letters
tight means drunk, so the letters of the word bay are reeling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recounts being overtaken while hemmed into a narrow bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' (drunk) jumbles the bay letters to ABY. The answer carries two senses at once: 'got' (obtained) and 'passed' (visited briefly).
explanation.definitionFit: To come by something is to obtain it, and to come by a place is to drop in or go past it.

clue.text: Easily moved about male priest getting media attention

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the light word goes round the others

parts.note: something light is easily lifted or moved
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: An impressionable male priest is thrust into the public eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the limelight means being the focus of public and press interest, from the old theatre spotlight.

clue.text: Sloth? One near it, trembling

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: trembling suggests the letters shaking loose and resettling in a new order

explanation.surface: A sloth hangs nearby, and someone close to it is shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the animal; the question mark admits it means laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as a vice means idleness, and inertia is a synonym for that sluggish reluctance to move.

clue.text: Celebrity and posh guy begin a meal?

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a toff is a British slang word for an upper-class man

explanation.surface: A famous figure and an aristocrat sit down to dine together.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh, upper-class person. The question mark flags a pun: a starter opens a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off is to begin, and the playful hint links it to the starter course of a meal.

clue.text: Seek arbiter for organising deciders

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a referee to set up the deciding matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-breakers are extra games or questions that settle a level contest, so they decide the winner.

clue.text: Cheese in bed, eaten by woman

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside, so the woman's name goes round the bed

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A woman eats soft cheese while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian cheese made from whey, an example of a cheese.

clue.text: External computer device failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the device's word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a router is a device that links computers to a network

explanation.surface: An outside piece of computer hardware won't boot up.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer and external are synonyms, both meaning on the outside.

clue.text: Food all right for so long

parts.note: fare means food, as in simple fare
well means in good health, all right

explanation.surface: Someone takes the food, confirms it is fine, and leaves for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal goodbye, and a farewell is a goodbye.

clue.text: Don't forget about departing politician

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so the about word goes from the longer word

parts.note: don't forget means remember
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A reminder about a politician who is leaving office.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is a politician, and member is short for that role.

clue.text: Cartographer in vehicle, on schedule coming back

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes car

indicators.note: coming back means the schedule word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A map-maker drives a car and arrives home on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish map-maker, famous for his map projection.

clue.text: One shouting loudly taking in Turin's original campanile

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the shouter goes round the letter

parts.note: someone who bellows is a bellower

indicators.note: original means the opening letter of the word Turin

explanation.surface: A loud shouter visits an old Italian bell tower in Turin.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is an Italian free-standing tower that houses bells.

clue.text: Union band

parts.note: looks like a trade union's brass band, but means the band of metal that marks a marriage union

explanation.surface: A trade union's musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a union, and the circular gold band worn to mark it is this ring.

clue.text: Cast the short line

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: An angler casts a shortened fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast and to throw are synonyms, as in casting a stone.

clue.text: Someone to watch over newspaper backer

parts.note: The Guardian is a British newspaper
an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show

explanation.surface: A newspaper's financial supporter keeps an eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a protective spirit, echoing the song Someone to Watch Over Me.

clue.text: Female independence in peril? Grow worried

indicators.note: worried means harassed or shaken about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is women's independence under threat? The anxiety rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Girl power is a slogan of women's self-reliance and empowerment, popularised by the Spice Girls.

clue.text: Account clergyman finds correct

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman checks the accounts and finds them right.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and correct are synonyms, both meaning free from error.

clue.text: King's wife and a prince rather put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are thrown into another order

explanation.surface: A queen and a prince are both somewhat annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's sixth and last wife was Catherine Parr, so she was a king's wife.

clue.text: Land mass area? US, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy here means to imagine freely, so these letters are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Someone muses on which huge region the United States might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe and Asia together form one continuous continent, the largest land mass on Earth.

clue.text: Set out from Scottish island, extremely game

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of the word game

explanation.surface: Someone sets out from a Scottish island to play a great game.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAN is an island off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to set them out in order, as with chairs or a display.

clue.text: Complied with demands, making love with you in part of garden

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: in means inside, putting the old word for you inside the flower patch

parts.note: a bed is a patch of a garden for plants
ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: A couple make love in a flower bed after yielding to a request.
explanation.definitionFit: To have obeyed is to have done as ordered, meaning following instructions given.

clue.text: Perfect state

definitions.meaning: to say or express in words

explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means total or complete; as a verb it means to speak or declare.

clue.text: Livener to take, short

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the take word loses its last letter

parts.note: to nick is to steal or take

explanation.surface: Someone needs a quick pick-me-up to knock back.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine or drink that invigorates, so it is something that livens you up.

clue.text: Dished roast up in GB bar

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the GB pair
dished means served up, so the letters are served in a new order

explanation.surface: A British pub serves up roasted dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub, or bar, known for serving high-quality food.

clue.text: Doubtful one acting so strangely

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic behaves in an odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who doubts whether God can be known is a religious sceptic, a doubtful person.

clue.text: Popular elsewhere, to some extent

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
away means somewhere else

explanation.surface: Someone is quite well liked in other places.
explanation.definitionFit: In a way is an idiom meaning partly, so it means to some degree.

clue.text: Former head of coven almost strung up in market

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the word coven
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: strung up means hanged

explanation.surface: A former leader of witches is lynched in a marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange is a place for trading, such as a stock or corn market.

clue.text: Grow furious in diocese with religious education beginning to decline

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
RE is the school subject Religious Education

indicators.note: beginning to means the opening letter of the word decline

explanation.surface: A bishop is enraged that religious teaching is falling away.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom meaning to become very angry.
